text:
The Fed didn't cut rates to zero in 2024. It began easing in September 2024 after holding the federal funds rate at 5.25-5.50% since July 2023. It cut 50 bp in September, 25 bp in November, and 25 bp in December, ending the year at 4.25-4.50%. The cuts came because inflation had cooled toward 2% and the labor market was softening, so the Fed was recalibrating away from a restrictive stance.

You may be thinking of the two times the Fed did move to near zero (0-0.25%): December 2008, during the financial crisis, and March 2020, in response to the COVID shock.

I can't speak reliably to 2025-2026 policy beyond what I know, so check the Fed's current target range if that matters to you.
